source.title: Field change for the Cassels–Tate pairing and applications to class groups
source.actually_read: Printed pp. 3–4 class reciprocity setup and Proposition 1.3; pp. 7–8 Cartier duality, Selmer-object local conditions and general pairing kernels; complete Sections 5.1–5.2, printed pp. 19–22, including Definition 5.2, Notation 5.3, all of Lemma 5.4 and Propositions 5.5–5.6 proofs, and the full deduction of Proposition 1.3. No fresh full proof of the preceding paper or the entire 46-page article is claimed.

correction.actually_read: Entire mathematical-purpose correction text on official publisher page: missing Alexander Smith affiliation only.

checks: Perfect reciprocity pairing is Cl-star times Cl, not an alternating class self-pairing.
Kummer Selmer group projects to Cl[p] with the unit kernel in (5.1); morphism g_m need not identify local conditions.
Proposition 5.6 requires roots of unity of order ab in the base and explicitly gives symmetry when a=b.
For a=b=p the actual Q(mu_p) and totally real quintic field do not contain mu_(p^2).
Even order-five alpha has odd Cartier dual omega*alpha^(-1), so there is no equivariant self-duality; a constant-target self-duality would require alpha^2=1.
A one-dimensional symmetric perfect pairing is algebraically possible; no even-length argument is supplied.
limits: No class-group vanishing or main-gate movement.
No assertion that all other possible pairings or arithmetic arguments are impossible.
